messages:
Maya: quick question — thinking about audit windowing granularity for billing events. do we keep minute-level windows, hour-level, or switch to event-level append-only?
Samir: curious what the motivating tradeoff is — storage & compute vs accuracy for late arrivals?
Maya: exactly. minute windows are nice for near-real-time dashboards, but makes reconciliation harder when replays/rewrites happen.
Alex: minute windows also blow up number of keys for multi-tenant billing. we saw >2x index size with current minute sharding in the prod snapshot.
Jen: on replays: our current backfill rewrites replace the windowed aggregates which is messy. we either need idempotent ingest or immutable event log + reconcile layer.
Samir: proposal: keep the ingest as append-only event stream (immutable events with sequence id), but expose aggregated views at configurable granularity (1m/1h/1d) computed by a separate job. That way replays only touch the event log, and aggregates can be recomputed lazily.
Maya: sounds good, but how do we handle near-real-time billing needs if aggregates are eventually consistent? some customers want <1s visibility.
Alex: we can keep a small in-memory sliding aggregator for hot tenants for real-time, and fall back to computed aggregates for historical accuracy. basically a hybrid: live cache + async durable aggregates.
Jen: also need to consider audit trails: auditors want to see the exact token-level attribution for a charged window. append-only event log gives that. we should include provenance headers on events (request_id, model_variant, routing_policy).
Samir: agree. event schema suggestion (short):
```
{event_id, tenant_id, ts, tokens_in, tokens_out, request_id, model, fallback_chain, source_zone}
```
Maya: nice. what about late-arrivals/out-of-order events? our watermark strategy today is conservative, but that leads to delayed charges.
Alex: watermarking with a bounded lateness (e.g., 5m) + tombstone semantics for deletes should cover most cases. For true replays that fix attribution, we require a replay API that tags events as replacements and provides mapping to previous event_ids.
Jen: and for audits we need an incremental reconcile API: provide window_id + since_token -> list of deltas. auditors can then request delta stream to validate re-calcs.
Samir: implementation note: aggregates should be computed with idempotent reducers and stored with append-only checkpoints so we can diff snapshots cheaply.
Maya: action items: Samir to draft event schema & replay API, Alex to prototype live cache + fallback, Jen to write audit delta API sketch. I'll consolidate into a short RFC.
Alex: +1. will check memory/gsnapshot implications for hot-tenant cache.
Jen: ping me when RFC draft is up, I'll add audit requirements.
Maya: thanks all. audit-bot: created ticket PERF-1423 for live cache prototype (link: https://issues.redwood/p/1423) :white_check_mark:
audit-bot: scheduled follow-up meeting for Mon 10am PT.
